position_outside: UN/LOCODE places East Port Said at (31.2167, 32.35), on the water just north-west of the terminal, about 500 m beyond these limits. The dredged channel there is the canal's Port Said bypass, which ships in transit use too, so the limits are not grown to take it in.

properties.source: Derived: the convex hull of this port's terminals from OpenStreetMap, grown by 300 m, then cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it (the sea within its coastline, rivers, docks and basins), with the terminals kept whole
properties.note: OpenStreetMap maps no port limits for East Port Said. These are the hull of the Suez Canal Container Terminal grown by 300 m, cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it, with the terminal kept whole and a 30 m margin where it meets the water: the terminal and its basin and berths, not the canal fairway's far bank or Port Fouad. A scan of OpenStreetMap finds no homes, residential land, schools, hospitals, places of worship or named places inside.

properties.name: SCCT
properties.note: The transhipment terminal on the east bank at the canal's northern entrance, known as SCCT. APM Terminals runs it. OpenStreetMap names it SCCT and tags it cargo=container.
